To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the DiP benchmark testsets and evaluation methods are the first to track discourse-related translation quality, and (2) the complex context-aware MT systems we test do not consistently outperform the simpler baseline systems on these tasks

(1) the MT systems tested in this study do not consistently improve discourse-related translations across languages and phenomena, and (2) we introduce the first MT benchmark testsets for tracking and evaluating discourse-related translations, and provide evaluation methods that can be used by future researchers.
the MT systems that we tested do not perform consistently well across discourse phenomena and that the MT systems with more complex context-aware architectures do not improve discourse translations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question: How do we evaluate MT systems for discourse phenomena?
the question whether and how MT systems should be evaluated on discourse phenomena.
evaluating MT systems in the presence of discourse phenomena and with identifying the best-performing MT systems in this regard.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we have introduced a benchmark for discourse phenomena in machine translation.
the MT systems that we test do a good job of translating discourse connectives, anaphora, and lexical consistency.
the current state of MT systems, even those that are context aware and use complex neural architectures, do not perform well on discourse phenomena.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

despite recent advances in neural machine translation (NMT) models that are able to leverage contextual information, the translation quality of discourse phenomena is still far from satisfactory, and that the current state-of-the-art models do not improve translation of discourse phenomena significantly over simpler baselines.
the current state-of-the-art MT models are not sensitive enough to capture the discourse phenomena in translation, and that the current metrics are not expressive enough for these phenomena.
we introduce a benchmark testset and evaluation method to track the quality of machine translation (especially for discourse-related phenomena).
The main takeaway from our work is that
discourse-related phenomena are not being adequately addressed in current MT systems.
MT systems are not able to translate discourse phenomena consistently better than a strong baseline.
the current generation of MT systems do not improve discourse translations consistently.
